The excerpt does not specify whether the authors re-analysed microdata with explicit student/sampling weights or whether they relied on OECD-produced estimates and figures. Because the report presents descriptive comparisons and regression-based associations (e.g., logistic and linear regression results) without detailing weight variables (such as W_FSTUWT/TOTWGT) or replicate-weight procedures, the weighting approach is not transparent in the provided text. For analysts replicating these results from PISA microdata, complex survey weights and replicate methods should be applied to account for clustering and unequal selection probabilities; however, the manuscript text does not report the exact weight variable names used.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD report analyses PISA 2018 to benchmark learning outcomes and describe how schooling policies and system features in the Western Balkans relate to performance and equity. It uses PISA’s representative sampling of 15-year-olds (grade 7 or above) and reports reading, mathematics and science outcomes, including proficiency levels and subgroup gaps by socio-economic status, gender, language of instruction, and educational track (general vs vocational). The report also draws on PISA questionnaires to describe school resourcing (material resources and technological infrastructure), school network characteristics (school size and student-teacher ratios), and teacher practices/quality assurance mechanisms (teacher-directed vs adaptive instruction, teacher appraisal, certification and professional development). Reported associations are typically based on regression models (e.g., logistic regression for track selection; linear regression for performance differences), but the excerpt does not provide a replicable ML specification, PV-combining rules, or missing-data procedure. Policy implications emphasise fairer student assessment and tracking, more equitable resourcing, and more holistic teacher appraisal and professional development aligned with desired teaching practices.
